before.explanation: The patient exhibits motor weakness and expressive dysphasia. The lesion is most likely in the left frontal lobe. : Vv Frontal Lobe ANATOMY / CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM

before.stem: ww Which of the following clinical features is most suggestive of a lesion of the parietal lobe:
warnings: No marked correct option was detected.
before.explanation: Hemispatial sensory neglect is most likely to be associated with damage to the parietal lobe. Receptive dysphasia may be seen in damage to the Wernicke speech area in the temporal lobe. Expressive dysphasia may be seen in damage to the Broca speech area in the frontal lobe. Contralateral motor weakness is due to damage of the motor cortex of the frontal lobe. Homonymous hemianopia is most likely to occur in damage of the occipital lobe. “ v

after.stem: Which of the following clinical features is most suggestive of a lesion of the parietal lobe:

after.explanation: Hemispatial neglect is strongly associated with parietal-lobe dysfunction, particularly in the non-dominant hemisphere.

after.highYieldNote: Hemispatial neglect is strongly associated with parietal-lobe dysfunction, particularly in the non-dominant hemisphere.

before.stem: ww Which of the following clinical features is most suggestive of a lesion of the temporal lobe:
options: Conjugate eye deviation towards the side of the lesion Srwrmanrenone
warnings: No marked correct option was detected.
before.explanation: Damage to the Wernicke's speech area in the temporal lobe can result in a receptive dysphasia. Hemispatial neglect is most likely to occur in a lesion of the parietal lobe. Homonymous hemianopia is most likely to occur in a lesion of the occipital lobe. Expressive dysphasia is most likely to occur in a lesion of the Broca speech area in the frontal lobe. Conjugate eye deviation towards the side of the lesion is most likely to occur in a lesion of the frontal lobe. “ v

before.stem: w Which of the following clinical features would you least expect to see in a lesion of the frontal lobe:
options: Primitive reflexes (x) Spastic paralysis of the contralateral leg 4% (Vv) Contralateral homonymous hemianopia with macular sparing 84%
warnings: No marked correct option was detected.
before.explanation: Contralateral homonymous hemianopia with macular sparing results from damage to the primary visual cortex of the occipital lobe. Incontinence may occur due to damage of the cortical micturition centre in the prefrontal cortex. Primitive reflexes and inability to problem solve may occur due to damage to the prefrontal cortex. Motor weakness of the contralateral limb with UMN signs may occur due to damage of the primary motor cortex. v
